rule: The studio feature and product cards show each brand's own canonical mark, copied byte for byte from its repository at a pinned commit. No mark is redrawn, retightened or recoloured here. Projects without a verified mark or public destination use their name and an honest development label. node scripts/sync-product-logos.mjs reproduces the pinned copies and --check fails on drift. Superseded entries are retained as history, never selected by the current catalog.

assets.decision: Owner-directed Québec F identity, revision 3 (scaleforged-website docs/brand/quebec-identity.md). The Québec silhouette takes the capital F position with a transparent F counterform; the light-surface fill is #24457F. It replaced the strike-F, retired 2026-10-19. The product publishes a portfolio-only derivative, quebec-mark-portfolio.svg, that scales the same paths about the ink centre so the province fills 96% of the 512 x 512 canvas instead of an app icon's 82%, which read undersized beside wordmark-led marks at 72 px. Only the group transform differs; the canonical symbol keeps 82% for app-icon and social use on scaleforged.io.

assets.source: Authored for this site, since no Lunorive logo file was available to copy. Glyph outlines come from Playfair Display Version 1.203 (SIL Open Font License 1.1), the site's display face, as next/font downloads it for this build: .next/static/media/eaead17c7dbfcd5d-s.p.woff2
assets.transformation: Typographic wordmark: the product name set in Playfair Display instanced at wght 700 with fontTools 4.65.0, kerned with the font's own GPOS pairs (i+v -4, v+e -15 units) and tracked -0.01em like the site's brand name, converted to outlines in ink #1b1714 with a terminal period in accent #d4831f. Not the storefront's own lettering, and no product imagery

The approved Empreinte package records stacked SCALE / FORGED lettering, vivid #FFD438 paper and #151714 ink. Brand/provenance.json in the source repository records the approved 2026-10-22 artwork and the 2026-10-24 vector trace. The final D in the canonical artwork is preserved.
